summary: Signed URL callback sequence causing late-window 429s and unclear quota allocation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 429 throttles that only appear ~8-20 minutes into their scheduled batch ingestion job. The job uses pre-signed upload URLs (signed by customer-supplied upload proxy) and an asynchronous callback to our API once the upload is committed. Behavior is new after they switched the ingest workers to a staggered fanout (short-lived workers per file) and upgraded to a higher concurrency pool.
Impact:
- Intermittent 429s causing downstream ingestion failures and retries; visible throughput drop during affected windows.
- Customer estimates ~12% of files fail and are retried, increasing cost and latency.
Environment:
- Customer account: NimbleDocs Inc (enterprise)
- Region: us-west primarily (failures also seen in us-east failover)
- Workload: scheduled batch uploader (staggered/fanout), uses signed URLs and ephemeral callback tokens from customer proxy
- Observed time: failures appear after 8–20 minutes into job and often cluster at 11:xx and 19:xx minute marks (mid-window).
Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start scheduled batch job with 500 concurrent short-lived workers (each worker obtains pre-signed URL and ephemeral callback token).
2) Workers upload to signed URL (S3-backed) and then call our /uploads/callback endpoint with callback token to finalize and trigger embedding generation.
3) After ~10 minutes, callbacks begin returning 429s from our API gateway; retries with exponential backoff sometimes succeed later.
Logs / snippets provided by customer:
- Gateway trace IDs (redacted): gtw-7b1d.. / gtw-7b1f.. showing 429s for POST /uploads/callback at 2026-03-01T11:10:12Z
- Customer-side note: "The worker that generated the signed URL sometimes finishes earlier; the callback is performed by a short-lived worker that holds a different ephemeral key than the original signer."
Additional notes from customer:
- They rotated ephemeral keys frequently (TTL 90s) to reduce blast radius.
- After temporarily reducing worker parallelism from 500->80, the 429s went away, suggesting concurrency/quota interaction.
Observations from support triage:
- Quota accounting appears to increment both on the signed URL registration route and again on the callback route in cases where the route is normalized differently (e.g., /uploads/callback?origin=proxy vs /uploads/callback).
- There is a hypothesis that ephemeral key fanout plus per-route token-bucket accounting leads to double-counting under certain connection reuse scenarios (HTTP/2 multiplexing or pooled proxy IPs).
- Related historical tickets show similar patterns when ephemeral keys or pooled proxies are used (linked: SUP-71234, SUP-553210).
steps_to_reproduce: Create 500 short-lived workers that each request a pre-signed URL and ephemeral callback token
Upload file to pre-signed URL (S3) and then POST to /uploads/callback with ephemeral token
Observe 429s around 8-20 minutes into the run, particularly when fanout and token rotation rates are high
logs:
[2026-03-01T11:10:12Z] POST /uploads/callback 429 xff=203.0.113.45 tid=gtw-7b1d status=429 quota=tenant:exhausted
[2026-03-01T11:10:12Z] POST /uploads/register 200 tid=gtw-7b1c req_id=abc123 ephemeral_key=ek-9a0f
[2026-03-01T11:10:13Z] POST /uploads/callback 200 tid=gtw-7b1e req_id=def456 ephemeral_key=ek-9a11 (on retry)
Note: customer provided full tracelog in support bundle (S3 link redacted) pointing to several different gateway worker instances and mixed connection pools.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Asha Patel (Support): Initial customer report received; triaging and requested full gateway traces and list of ephemeral key TTLs.

2026-03-02 — Diego Martinez (SRE): Observed that quota service logs show two increments within the same logical flow when callback token and original upload request present different route-keys. Filed hypothesis: route-normalization mismatch + ephemeral-key fanout => misattributed token consumption. Linking quota-service PRs for awareness.

2026-03-03 — NimbleDocs (Customer): Confirmed tokens were rotated every 90s and that callbacks originate from separate short-lived processes not reusing original connection. Lowering concurrency reduces failures; provided additional pcap of proxy IP pooling.

2026-03-04 — Diego Martinez (SRE): Reproduced locally with test harness that simulates signed-url + callback. Able to trigger double-counting when callback uses different query param order; created mitigation plan to add consistent route canonicalization in gateway and a temporary console toggle for per-route isolation for this customer.

2026-03-05 — Asha Patel (Support): Communicated workaround to customer (reduce worker fanout or enable per-route isolation toggle); engineering to deploy a canonicalization hotfix in staging and schedule production rollout if tests pass.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Quota accounting double-increments when equivalent routes are not canonicalized before token-bucket lookup (e.g., query param order, trailing slash, origin param).
Hypothesis 2: Pooled proxy IPs + HTTP/2 multiplexing cause per-connection attribution mismatches between upload registration and callback, leading to tenant-wide token exhaustion spikes.
Evidence: Reproduction harness triggers same 429 pattern when callback path is mutated (added ?origin=proxy) and ephemeral keys are rotated rapidly.
Short-term mitigation: advise customer to reduce parallel short-lived workers, increase ephemeral TTL, or use a single long-lived callback agent per batch.
resolution: Workaround provided: temporary console toggle 'per-route-quota-isolation' turned ON for NimbleDocs; suggested reductions to ephemeral key rotation and worker parallelism. Engineering identified a bug in gateway route canonicalization that can cause duplicate quota increments for the same logical flow. Fix (normalize query params and path) is implemented in github.com/redwood/ingest-service/pull/428 and under test in staging. Target prod rollout: 2026-03-10 behind feature flag. Post-deploy: monitor tenant token consumption metrics for 48h, then advise customer on reverting temporary toggle.
next_steps: Deploy canonicalization fix to staging and run full batch ingest regression tests
Coordinate with account team to keep per-route isolation toggle enabled until quota patterns are stable
After prod rollout, run 48h monitoring and close ticket if no recurrence
If recurrence appears, consider server-side de-dup of quota increments by request fingerprint
customer_communication: 2026-03-04: Sent interim workaround and toggle instructions; customer applied and reported immediate drop in 429s at lower concurrency (NimbleDocs)
2026-03-05: Notified customer of planned staging rollout and tentative prod date; requested availability window for final verification
